notes.title: Devblog #3 - The Heart of the Inn - Mastering the Kitchen
notes.content:
Greetings, Innkeepers!

It’s time we returned with news of Crossroads Inn 2. We realize it’s been a while since last updates, but with intense game development underway, it was very challenging to spare any time at all.

Much has changed since our previous devblog: mechanics have evolved, systems got refined, and new features have been added. In the months ahead, we will take you through the newest additions. Today, we begin with the heart of every great inn — the kitchen.

Meeting culinary needs

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/84584f1ea337b16bcca440abe61bc276b095b63f.gif
We gave a new meaning to cooking in the game - now different guests come with varied palates to be satisfied. Depending on who is visiting your inn - their background and social group level - they will have different needs and preferences. If you do well, then they will likely stay at your inn longer, raise their happiness level, spend more guldens and interact with other guests. More on guests another time though! Let’s get to cooking.

Crafting dishes

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/cdf6b686f585b60223754a837ff57e3f600c804e.gif
Every dish consists of at least 2 mandatory ingredients. In some recipes you can add up to 4 ingredient slots in total. Those 2 extra ingredient slots come with additional functionality - they add more quality or traits (or both) to the recipe. The recipe itself can already come with some traits and it always has a base quality.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/72547056544a6552b21e675be0f934bb04d4c582.gif
The dish can have up to 3 traits. The more traits you overlap with certain guests preferences, the more bonus you gain for catering to their taste. There are different guests who can be satisfied with a single well-balanced dish, so it pays off to pay attention to what your patrons are interested in! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/cf0f193c8d062e7bff10f44f561dda8d5a98a604.gif
In the future, we want the dish traits to also influence guests social reactions, like for example being more sleepy from having a hearty dish or developing a need for a drink after a salty one. This way, if done correctly, you could steer your guests into staying overnight and spending more guldens on drinks.

Unlocking ingredients & recipes

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/2f9bd23815c486fe3414d9742c4ff3523147186c.gif
You obviously start with some basic recipes, something like beer and bread to get you going. As you progress with different Backgrounds (Guest types), you unlock more and more recipes and also gain Regional Influence which allows you to unlock much needed ingredients. Ingredients have different quality values that can be run down by spoilage - and in the end influence the overall quality score of the dish - so it is essential to keep your produce fresh.

Farming DLC

In the future, we are planning to add DLC with possibility to grow your own vegetables and raise farm animals. This way, you would not have to rely on market prices and you could get the freshest and highest quality ingredients from your very own backyard.

notes.title: Devblog #2 - The Road to Crossroads Inn 2
notes.content:
Greetings, innkeepers! After announcing Crossroads Inn 2 a year ago, we're still on the journey to its release and excited to share our progress with you. Despite the challenges facing the gamedev market, we've weathered the storm and continue to make steady progress. Today, we'd like to give you a brief update on what we've been working on, which will be followed by more detailed devblogs for each area.

Core Features

We've been focusing our efforts on developing and refining the essential elements of the inn management experience:
[olist]
1.  Code and Game Architecture: It’s the heart of our game, ensuring it’s great now and will stay that way. This is why with Crossroads Inn 2 we continuously improve stability to ensure that it won’t be a buggy mess but a smooth, enjoyable experience.

2. Building and Furnishing: In CINN 2, we’ve introduced Creation Mode—a complete system that lets you build, furnish, decorate, and manage external structures. It’s the core of your inn-keeping journey. We’ve fine-tuned this mode to provide better feedback while maintaining creative freedom and ensuring everything works seamlessly.

3. NPC’s AI: We’ve made your staff and guests smarter and more responsive, creating a more immersive experience. You’ll have a clear understanding of why your workers behave the way they do, and you’ll be able to influence their actions, both directly and indirectly.

4. Inn Management: Whether it’s crafting menus and selecting dishes, managing workers, or ensuring guest satisfaction, we’ve enhanced and intertwined every aspect of inn management to deliver a more immersive and engaging experience.

5. Resource Management and Crafting: We’ve refined the systems for purchasing, crafting ingredients, and managing storage, giving you greater control over your inn’s resources. How you use these resources to craft dishes will directly influence your guests’ satisfaction and judgments.

6. Guest Feedback: We’ve enhanced the way guests communicate their needs, satisfaction, and reviews, giving you clearer insights into your inn’s performance. You’ll have access to all the information left by your patrons, allowing you to continually improve and adapt to their evolving expectations.

[/olist]
Looking Ahead

There are still many systems in design and development that we’re not quite ready to fully reveal. For instance, we’re currently working on a new tag system for building and decorating that will add even more depth to the Building and Furnishing experience. However, we’re thrilled with the visual and technical improvements we’ve made so far, and we’re excited to share some in-game footage showing off the current state of the game’s visuals:

Lighting Update

We introduced volumetric lighting system to the game which enables us to have a more immersive feeling of natural light, mimicking dust particles in the air. We’re still working on refining the system under different angles and dynamic outside lighting situation, but we’re on a good track to create a richer, cosy feeling to the atmosphere of the tavern.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/b706ce376d0c423bd2cc65d5aa258622dc227c78.gif
Placing windows gives a cone of light

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/8c8d1e0b7cc4cb18f02884cfffc4da76c20298fb.gif
Placing lighting enhances the volumetrics of both light sources

Guest NPCs Update

We managed to update the game with a wide variety of different Guest NPCs - people of different regions, genders and social status that will be reflected on their clothing and preferences. More complex animations are still in the works, but we can already enjoy a more vibrant and colorful inn full of diverse guests.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/efd838433d12657b1367f07d95a993e88708bba1.gif

Worker NPCs Update

We are also aiming to keep the workers diverse and easy to be noticed among crowds of guests - some of our ideas are already implemented - like tall hats for cooks and head covers for servers in order for them to be recognized from a distance. We will work further on more engaging animation for taking orders, cooking and various idles. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/02764eb1e030d89ce64eccf945014bb47e6e51f7.gif

New Wall & Floor Textures

As we keep adding new content and assets to the game, we try to upgrade the visuals even more each time. With the new light support, here come also some new textures for the walls and floors of your inn.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/25b1c3f6b7b2ab409b131ab3ffbee88bf7c38f1c.gif

Meet The Team

As we continue our journey with Crossroads Inn 2, we’d like to take a moment to introduce ourselves. The team working on CINN 2 is a fresh and passionate group, dedicated to bringing out the best of the Crossroads Inn legacy. Our core team consists of just four members—Robert (production, game design), Nikita (programming, system design), Maja (art direction, 2D art concepts), and Łukasz (QA and sound design)—but we’ve been fortunate to have the support of many talented individuals over the past year. These include Maxime (game design, UI/UX design), Thibaut (game design), Adam (writer and narrative designer), Daria (3D character artist), Marcos (3D artist), Ola (2D UI artist), Denis (programmer), Michał (tech artist), and Ola (animator), all of whom have made significant contributions as part of our team.

While we are a new team, we carry a deep respect for the original Crossroads Inn. We’ve embraced the heritage of the game and are committed to making CINN 2 a great experience that builds on what players loved while avoiding the pitfalls of the past. We’re excited to bring a fresh perspective, learning from the past, and striving to create an even more engaging and polished experience for all of you.

Thank you for your continued support and patience. We can't wait to share more updates with you as we get closer to release!

notes.title: Devblog #1: UI and UX
notes.content:
Hi Folks! It's been a while since the announcement and we're ready to share some new details about the sequel to Crossroads Inn!


In today’s dev blog, we’d like to share the main goals and inspirations for the UI/UX design in Crossroads 2. 


When we started designing the interface we knew that we needed to improve on the UI from the original game. We wanted it to be more functional and clearer in conveying information and feedback that the player needs. However, we wanted it to retain a Mediaeval-like feeling, so that it remains in line with the game and the general visual aspects of it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/7be99a54afdff3ff816c831f44a1d5a073aa2b84.jpgCrossroads Inn vs. Crossroads Inn 2

As you can see, the new UI design is lighter, and smoother, while also being much clearer as to its functionality, details of objects, and so on.

Main Inspirations

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/d487c55254cb6e299733135b92845d01f9693759.jpg

As it often happens during a creative process, we went to some of our favourite games to find inspiration for the new UI. First of them was Anno 1800. With its clear division of elements of the UI, it creates a functional system that’s not obscuring the game itself, while the colours, textures, and slight decorations create a visual feeling bringing the setting to life.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/5630f3b901d4ea522dabe5695590fcceeb7d2540.jpg

While completely different in mood, Two Point Campus is another of our inspirations. The UI is not overly stylized and it conveys all the important feedback and information in a clear way, never leaving the player wondering what exactly is going on and where, how, and what they can do.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/8a55fd35450e166afaf7d1b2d5206915876237df.png

Another game worth a mention is The Witcher: Monster Slayer. While it’s a game aimed at a different platform, the use of clearly defined icons and brackets, combined with aptly chosen textures and ornaments, creates a perfectly clear and yet climactic UI.

New Look

There are a couple of things that we wanted to change from the UI design of Crossroads Inn, and one of those is the colours - and textures. We also wanted to avoid design choices typical for most Mediaeval-set games wherein choices of colours and textures create a very heavy and morose atmosphere. 

There is no denying that that does fit many games, but in case of Crossroads Inn 2 we wanted the UI to be something that’s pleasing to look at not just within the setting of the game, but also aside from it, for when the player needs to forget for a moment about world immersion and focus on purely managerial, technical, and strategic elements.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/60c5dd579b8dae8edbaec117b0272b5606cd5246.jpg
Colour palette and textures.

Of course, keeping the Mediaeval tone of the UI was still very important for us. But to make it lighter, we decided to avoid overabundance of dark colours or metal and stone textures. Instead, we chose beige and dark, navy blue, combined with paper, wood, and textile textures. We’ve also added some Medieval-inspired ornamental patterns to finally achieve a clear, functional, but also era-appropriate UI. 

And, since the art direction is overseeing UI, 2D, and 3D graphics, it all fits together nicely, having been designed together simultaneously from the start.

Functionality

Taking into consideration all that we’ve learned from Crossroads Inn, and with new people on the team bringing new ideas, we’ve decided to step away from the UI of the original game which seemingly favoured visuals over functionality. The visuals themselves also did not fit our vision for Crossroads Inn 2, so, in the end, we went in a completely different direction, creating a much clearer UI that makes the navigation much easier, while making the visuals equally stylized, but in a more complex fashion.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/89322dd129b891f0d27815a70b18ac4b927a4eda.jpg
Placing furniture in Crossroads Inn and Crossroads Inn 2.

As you can see, the UI is much clearer, while also offering much more data and feedback to the player.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/48bf93348fa76239686e32741f4d8b3907e1a571.jpg
Guest list and guest details in Crossroads Inn and Crossroads Inn 2.

Aside from offering more information, the design ideas behind the new UI included avoiding creating empty spaces often present in the UI windows from the first game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/f7f75fb8cfcc4380911d8b82873d2368875a9093.jpg
Worker list and details (and worker promotion window) in Crossroads Inn and Crossroads Inn 2.

As it’s been said - more details, more data, everything much clearer.

And last, but not least: event windows:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/ca1b505a357ef5a1bba7ea0233590fe9378204ea.jpg
Crossroads Inn and Crossroads Inn 2 events.

Again - less empty space, clearer, and stylistically pleasing.

Art Direction

According to Maja, our Art Director, the aim of the design team and the art direction is ‘to create a unified but unique feeling of all the artistic aspects of the game - UI, 3D assets, and 2D illustrations. We are trying to find a sweet spot between the gray and grim medieval world and colorful and free realm of fantasy.’ 

Thanks to this clear vision, Crossroads Inn 2’s visuals are all working in tandem, bringing to life the same vision of the world, no matter if it’s through the guests that arrive in the inn, the graphics representing different elements, or the interface through which the player navigates.

…and that’s it for today’s blog! Thank you for reading and if you have any questions, feedback, or opinions, we’ll be thrilled to read them. The comments section belongs to you! 


And keep an eye out for our next dev blog - there’s a lot more that we’d like to share with you! 

We've got one more thing, Here are some questions you've often asked:

FAQ:
Question: Is the new system going to be more responsive than in the previous game?
Answer: Yes, one of our main goals was to make the UI clear and intuitive, while also providing the player with all the feedback they may need.

Question: Have you improved the readability of text from the original Crossroads Inn?
Answer: Yes, it was one of the more important items on our Fix-It list, since it is a management game with narrative elements, meaning the player needs all the information and feedback served in the most coherent way possible.

Join us on Discord where you can ask devs directly about Crossroads Inn 2: https://discord.gg/gmrTUWsgpq

notes.title: Welcome to Crossroads Inn 2
notes.content:
Hi! Today we’d like to announce Crossroads Inn 2, a real-time management simulation game where the player takes on the role of an innkeeper in a fantasy world. Build, manage, and make choices that will affect your business, your story - and maybe the whole continent.

Creative Freedom

In Crossroads Inn 2, we've taken the building and furnishing systems to the next level. The completely redesigned functionalities not only create a more seamless and intuitive design experience, but they also help avoid potential pitfalls that could impact the smooth running of your inn. The rooms themselves are divided into different types, each with its own functions, while your furnishing choices may affect the guests, their satisfaction, and your general popularity among different social groups.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/df60f69787dbd5d3e5f27f4f48c0552f0868d1e8.gif

Crossroads Inn 2 takes a significant leap forward with our transition from the Esenthel engine to Unity. This transformative change allows us to refine and expand on various gameplay aspects, including ergonomics, pathfinding, and NPC behaviours. The shift to Unity also provides a more fluid and responsive experience when it comes to objects and interactions on the grid where the true magic of Crossroads Inn 2 comes to life.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/730ab837880b836a4537ecd66beb575032e232d4.gif

Art of Management

In Crossroads Inn 2, we have entirely re-envisioned the NPC system to create more believable, diverse characters. The new system enables these characters to make intelligent decisions influenced by the environment you've created and your skilful inn management. This interactivity adds depth to the gameplay and makes your guests' needs more evident - and fulfilling them is the cornerstone of the game. The menu, the services you provide, the style and quality of your inn - it all matters!

Our enhancements extend to the most essential NPCs - your workers - too. The revamped system provides a more transparent overview of your staff’s activities and highlights areas needing your attention as a clever innkeeper. By investing time in managing your workers wisely, you elevate your inn's ability to meet customer demands, creating an unmatched hospitality experience in your tavern.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/a343631f4f66a2eb37f7414ddd1e9ebafae7b35d.jpg

Living World

On top of all that, we have decided to go above and beyond our game's core element - the living world and its unfolding story. In Crossroads Inn 2, you develop your innkeeper character and gameplay style your way, choosing the path that suits you best. Whether you wish to focus solely on mastering the art of management, or you aspire to be a savvy entrepreneur who knows everything about the world's events and how to cleverly interact with them, the choice is yours. Immerse yourself in a life of an innkeeper in a world where your actions truly matter.

Art Direction

The main idea behind the art direction in our sequel is to put a stronger emphasis on semi-realistic fantasy visuals, and to have them correspond with the game mechanics. For example, given how the continent of Delcrys is made of three different countries (Yorevale, Untermarch, and Sambria), we want the citizens of each of them to have their own, instantly recognizable colour schemes and style. The styling of those will be based on different real-life cultures, from medieval Nordic and Slavic fashion to early Renaissance French, German, and Italian looks and trends.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44304953/4025dc335a8b56d12fcaba2817b4172f130b44cd.jpg

UI

Creating UI for a tycoon and/or simulation game is never an easy task. The most challenging part is giving the player a lot of different options - there’s walls to be built, furniture to be set, people to hire, people to welcome, and so on - while also making it clear and coherent from the get-go. So, while the UI in the original Crossroads Inn was sometimes a bit cumbersome, we’re taking all that we’ve learned to heart to make it all more clear, while also keeping the game mechanics, and even improving on those.

Sound Design

Since Crossroads Inn is all about recreating the life of an innkeeper in late-medieval/early Renaissance (with a dash of fantasy, of course), we needed the sound to be rather diverse. First, we need the outside of the inn, the sound of wind, trees, etc., which invoke feelings of calm and progress; not being too intrusive, but always being there, as it’s in real life, even if we don’t notice it. But there is more to that - we have a day and night cycle, different regions with their own atmosphere, and we want it all to be represented by sound - and music. An inn has to have music, after all! 

And that’s it - for now! We’ll have a lot more to share with you in the future, near and distant, but we want you all to know that our passionate team is working hard and can’t wait to show you what Crossroads Inn 2 will be all about!
